thread.title: Players revelling in return of Roddy Gayle Jr. to Michigan
thread.title_full: Players revelling in return of Roddy Gayle Jr. to Michigan

author: Gabe Miller
title: Players revelling in return of Roddy Gayle Jr. to Michigan
text:
With four portal acquisitions primed to play significant time on the court, not many Michigan men’s basketball players can claim last year’s national championship ring. But Thursday, that group got a little bit bigger.
After being granted a preliminary injunction to embrace his newfound eligibility, graduate guard Roddy Gayle Jr. is back in Ann Arbor. It wasn’t without roadblocks, though, as a freshly-minted amendment to the restraining order was needed for him to circumvent NCAA restrictions on rostered professionals, due to Gayle already playing for the Detroit Pistons during NBA Summer League.
But now he — and consequently his championship-caliber wisdom — is back, and Michigan couldn’t be happier to hear it.
“I’m ecstatic to have him back on the squad,” freshman forward Quinn Costello said at Michigan Media Day. “He’ll be a leader for sure. I work out with him all the time, and (I) learn something new every time. … (He’s) a guy you can go to if you need guidance.”
As one of few returners to play competitive minutes, Gayle helps to anchor the team with his seniority — but he’s not just a player-coach. Averaging 7.3 points per game, he shined in the postseason, dropping 16 points against No. 4 seed Alabama in the Sweet 16 en route to cutting down the nets in the national championship.
“We do a little gratitude circle at the end of practice a couple times a week, and many of those guys talk about their gratitude for Roddy and his maturity, his work ethic, his mentality,” Wolverines coach Mike Boynton Jr. said.
Gayle’s return is well-timed, as the Wolverines’ have multiple injury-sprung leaks in the backcourt already. Freshman guard Brandon McCoy Jr. tore his ACL during Michigan’s preseason games in Europe, and more recently against Oregon State , freshman guard Joseph Hartman went down for a couple weeks with a shoulder injury.
“Having (Gayle) to offset (McCoy’s injury),” Boynton said. “He’s not Brandon, like very different players. But similar, right? Big wings who can play two ways, and Roddy’s obviously got a little bit of an experience advantage.”
While Gayle doesn’t compensate one to one for lost lethality, he more than makes his crust while on defense. Filling in at the rim or on the perimeter when needed, his versatility lends itself to breaking offensive rhythm, and his size allows him to effectively cover most people he’s asked to. As Michigan often cycles ‘1’-through-‘4’ defensively, it can rest easy knowing that Gayle will size up to his man, no matter the position.
Gayle’s ring-bearing brothers-in-arms are also ready to go back to work with him.
“(Gayle’s return) helps us a lot, especially defensively,” senior guard Elliot Cadeau said. “He’s a very experienced guard, and he’s really good at playing defense. … One of our biggest problems in scrimmages has been defense, so we think he’ll bring another level to this team.”
Due to the delayed amendment, Gayle hasn’t seen any action on the court yet. While he played four summer games with the Pistons, he practiced with the Wolverines throughout the summer, extending into fall, as well. His dynamic with fellow players has been well documented, but a revamped interior also gives Gayle new opportunities. As a team, the Wolverines have harped on their perimeter-oriented approach, an approach Gayle can supplement with his 31.8% completion from the arc last season.
But for now, questions about chemistry or schemes can take a backseat. Michigan is simply happy to have a familiar face back on the bench.
